issues.legal_issue: A lease permitting continued occupation for an indefinite period is not perpetual unless its terms clearly make the leasehold interest heritable.
material_facts: The lease was made to allow construction of a residential building and specified an initial fixed term.
It allowed the lessee to remain in possession after that term while paying the agreed rent, which the lessor could not increase.
The lease allowed the lessee or heirs to remove the building in specified circumstances and allowed transfer of the building, but did not clearly make the leasehold interest heritable.
issues.conclusion: The lease lasted for the initial fixed term and, if the lessee remained in possession afterwards, for the lessee’s lifetime; it did not create a perpetual or hereditary interest.
issues.legal_principle: A lease must be construed as a whole to determine whether the parties intended a permanent interest. An indefinite term ordinarily lasts for the lessee’s lifetime unless the lease clearly shows an intention to make the interest hereditary; transferability alone does not make it heritable. The Court relied on Sivayogeswara Cotton Press v. Panchaksharappa, which approved the approach in Bavasaheb v. West Patent Company, and distinguished that case because the lease there expressly bound the parties’ heirs and successors. It also discussed Abdul Rahim v. Sarafalli and Lekhraj Roy v. Kunhya Singh.

predicates.civil_appeal_on_leasehold_land_claims: The proceeding is a civil appeal involving the duration of a leasehold interest in land.
predicates.building_lease: The parties made the lease for the purpose of constructing a building.
predicates.continued_occupation_at_fixed_rent: The lease allowed the lessee to remain in possession indefinitely after its initial term while paying an unchanged rent.
predicates.no_clear_hereditary_grant: The lease did not clearly provide that the leasehold interest would pass to the lessee’s heirs as a continuing interest.
predicates.transferability_without_hereditary_terms: The lease allowed a transfer of the building or leasehold interest but did not state that the interest was hereditary.

issues.definition: When a building lease allows continued occupation at fixed rent but does not clearly make the interest hereditary, the lease is limited to the original lessee’s lifetime.

issues.legal_issue: A lessee claiming that neighboring land became an accession to the lease must establish acquisition of that land by adverse possession during the lease.
material_facts: The claimant said a strip adjoining the leased land was either included in the lease or had become an accession to it.
The strip was demarcated as part of a separate plot, and neither the claimant nor his predecessor objected to that demarcation.
The claimant’s evidence concerned building eaves and windows, a drain, and use of the strip as a passage; he did not establish that these uses were acts of adverse possession over the strip.
The claimant testified that the strip was covered by the original lease, rather than acquired in addition to the leased land.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not establish that the strip had been acquired as an accession by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 108(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, an accession made to leased property during the lease is treated as part of the lease; where a lessee acquires land by encroachment and prescription, it is held for the benefit of the tenancy during the lease and thereafter for the lessor. The claimant must establish the alleged adverse acquisition. The Court accepted the Letters Patent Bench’s assessment of the evidence and held that the claimant’s ownership-based account and evidence of easementary use did not prove adverse possession.

predicates.civil_appeal_on_leasehold_land_claims: The proceeding is a civil appeal involving a claim that neighboring land formed part of a leasehold.
predicates.neighboring_land_claimed_as_lease_access: The claimant asserted that land adjoining the leased property had become part of the leasehold as an accession.
predicates.no_proof_of_adverse_acquisition: The claimant did not establish that the land was acquired through adverse possession or encroachment.
predicates.separate_demarcation_unopposed: The land was demarcated as a separate parcel and the claimant and predecessor did not object.
predicates.claimant_described_land_as_originally_le: The claimant’s evidence treated the land as having been included in the original lease rather than acquired later.

issues.definition: When a claimant asserts accession but does not prove adverse acquisition, and the evidence treats the land as originally leased despite an unopposed separate demarcation, the accession claim is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A person who exercised a claimed right on the footing that the land was their own cannot establish that same use as a prescriptive easement over another’s land after failing to establish ownership.
material_facts: The claimant maintained in evidence that the strip was included in the lease and that his rights over it arose under the lease, not later.
He did not claim that he had exercised the disputed rights on the footing that the strip belonged to someone else.
The claimant failed to establish that the strip was included in the lease or acquired as an accession.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not rely on the same use to establish prescriptive easements after failing to prove his claim that the strip was part of his leased land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12 and 15 of the Easements Act govern who may acquire an easement and the method of acquisition. A prescriptive easement requires a conscious, hostile exercise of the claimed right over another person’s property. A claimant may plead ownership and easement in the alternative, but use exercised on the footing of ownership is not use as an easement. The Court relied on Rayachand v. Maniklal. It noted conflicting High Court views in Abdul Rashid v. Brahman Saron and Ambaram v. Budhalal on a lessee’s ability to acquire certain easements, but found it unnecessary to resolve that conflict.

predicates.civil_appeal_on_land_and_easement_claims: The proceeding is a civil appeal involving a claim to land and an alternative claim to easementary rights over it.
predicates.prescriptive_easement_claim: The claimant sought to establish an easement based on long use.
predicates.claimant_asserted_land_was_their_own_or_: The claimant maintained that the land was owned or leased by them, rather than treating it as another person’s property.
predicates.no_conscious_use_as_another_persons_land: The claimant did not establish a conscious exercise of the claimed right over land understood to belong to someone else.
predicates.ownership_claim_failed: The claimant failed to prove that the land was theirs or included in their lease.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks a prescriptive easement but exercised the use as if the land were their own, without conscious use of another person’s land, that use does not establish an easement after the ownership claim fails.

issues.legal_issue: Use of another person’s land as a passage does not establish a prescriptive easement when the use was permissive or was not proved to be uninterrupted use as of right for the required period.
material_facts: The claimant used the strip as a passage to reach a well on the other plot and a structure that had stood there under a separate tenancy.
The claimant and his predecessor had permission to draw water from the well, and the passage use was incidental to that permission.
The claimant acknowledged the separate tenancy and rent for the structure on the other plot.
The evidence did not establish continuous, uninterrupted use of the strip as a passage as of right for the statutory period.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not acquire a prescriptive right of passage over the strip.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the Easements Act requires access or use as an easement, without interruption, for the prescribed period. The enjoyment must be as of right and not permissive under a licence or agreement. The Court concluded that the passage use was permissive and therefore could not establish the claimed easement.

predicates.civil_appeal_on_easement_claims: The proceeding is a civil appeal involving a claim to acquire an easement by long use.
predicates.passage_easement_claimed_by_prescription: The claimant sought a right of passage based on use over time.
predicates.passage_use_was_permissive_or_not_proved: The passage use was allowed as a matter of permission or was not proved to have been uninterrupted use as of right for the required period.

issues.definition: When a passage easement is claimed by prescription but the use was permissive or was not proved to be uninterrupted use as of right, the prescriptive passage easement is not established.

issues.legal_issue: Obstruction of light or air through a building’s openings is actionable only when it causes substantial deprivation of the legally protected kind.
material_facts: Construction on the neighboring land partly obstructed light and air through some windows on the building’s ground and first floors; windows on the second floor were unaffected.
The building also had doors and windows on the opposite side.
The claimant did not prove that the obstruction substantially deprived the building of light or air or made its occupation uncomfortable.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not establish an actionable obstruction of light or air.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33 of the Easements Act requires substantial damage to establish a suit for disturbance of an easement. Under its explanations, interference with light must materially diminish the value of the dominant heritage, and interference with air must materially affect the plaintiff’s physical comfort. A mere reduction in light or air is insufficient; the deprivation must be substantial. The Court relied on Colls v. Home and Colonial Stores.

predicates.civil_appeal_on_light_or_air_easement_cl: The proceeding is a civil appeal involving a claim that construction disturbed an easement of light or air.
predicates.construction_obstructed_some_openings: Construction on neighboring land reduced light or air through at least some openings in the claimant’s building.
predicates.substantial_deprivation_not_proved: The claimant did not prove substantial deprivation of light or air of the kind that materially affects the building’s value or the occupant’s physical comfort.

issues.definition: When neighboring construction obstructs some openings but substantial deprivation is not proved, an actionable disturbance of light or air is not established.
